correctness.rationale: A full derivation begins from an explicit properly normalized W_2(d,[[2,1],[1,2]]) density. The Gram-to-length-and-included-angle Jacobian is 4x^2y^2 sin(gamma); the sine-law Jacobian is t sin(gamma). Integrating the resulting t^(2d-1) exp(-t^2 Q/6) density by the gamma integral and duplication identity yields the precise factor (d-1)2^(d-1)3^(d/2)/pi. The independent Z,W Gaussian diagonalization gives exact mutually independent H~Beta(d/2,d/2), T~chi-square(2d), and J~sphere-direction cosine, plus explicit equalities for all three squared sides. The event gamma>pi/2 is exactly H<1/4. A one-sided beta Laplace analysis proves d Delta=>Exp(1); spherical and chi-square CLTs prove independent Gaussian leg and scale components. The cosine law with conditional concentration x/d,y/d->3/2 and T/d->2 yields d(gamma-pi/2)=>2 Exp(1). Numerical integrations and checked exact coordinate identities supplement, not replace, these infinite-dimensional and all-dimensional arguments.
risks: All asymptotic statements are weak limits without error rates; the numerical checker does not certify a proof.

originality.rationale: Finch 2014 explicitly writes the exact angular formula as a conjecture; the proposal is not new, but a proof and the joint conditional rare-event scaling are the proposed contributions. Edelman-Strang 2015 already derives the beta one-side law and obtuse probabilities and gives a planar angle-Jacobian sketch. Those facts are fully credited, and they do not explicitly state the joint conditional independence of obtuse excess, leg imbalance, and total scale. An earlier source covering the joint scaling could overturn priority. The unread 1996 Eisenberg-Sullivan article is a material, explicitly unresolved risk.
residual_risks: Eisenberg and Sullivan (1996) full text inaccessible; a stronger general angle/shape theorem there might alter historical priority.
The angular formula was an explicit pre-existing conjecture, not an independently discovered formula.

value.rationale: The joint angular probability law was an explicit natural conjecture for Gaussian triangles, making its proof independently motivated. In high dimensions obtuseness is exponentially rare, and conditioned triangles concentrate near right angles. The theorem pinpoints three natural and jointly independent fluctuation coordinates: dimension-scaled obtuse excess, root-dimension leg asymmetry, and root-dimension radial scale. This adds geometric information unavailable from the already known obtuseness probability or a one-dimensional beta side marginal. There is no arbitrary parameter slice or purely numerical benchmark; each quantity corresponds to a natural component of the conditioned triangle shape.
risks: The precise rate of convergence remains unquantified; the theorem is not claimed to yield an application outside geometric probability.
